subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 02, 2026
body:
Subject: Calamares config now boots at 1080p, ships without forced disk encryption

Two quiet but meaningful commits landed in the AcreetionOS Calamares config today. Darren (cobra3282000) pushed a fix that prefers the 1080p gfxmode over native 4K during boot, which should make installer screens render sanely on 4K panels that previously looked like a pixelated mess. The same batch also dropped forced disk encryption from the default install path, with a note that users can add it later if they want it. Both changes are already reflected in the live config tree over on the GitLab.

Development

The gfxmode change is the kind of fix nobody notices until it does its job, then everyone notices when it breaks. Plenty of users on 4K laptops were getting stretched, blurry GRUB output on first boot; preferring 1080p gives a sharp framebuffer that the installer and early userspace can rely on. The encryption change is more philosophical: AcreetionOS has always leaned toward privacy by choice rather than privacy by surprise, and not gating the first install behind a LUKS passphrase is consistent with that. Power users who want full-disk encryption can still set it up post-install with a single pacman call. If you want the exact package versions and patch context, the running notes live on the changelog at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Community

Firefox 155 shipped upstream and is already rolling into our repos, and Tuesday's security batch covered a wide spread of distros including Debian's expat and libdbd-csv fixes worth watching if you run mixed-arch systems. LWN also ran another one of those "please subscribe" notes this week, which is the internet's equivalent of a building's "support your local library" sign. Worth a coffee if you read them often. New contributors poking at AcreetionOS tooling can start from the docs at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html and the project landing at https://acreetionos.org/.

Tip of the day

If you grabbed the previous ISO and got a fuzzy GRUB on a 4K panel, reflash from the current build on the flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html. The new gfxmode kicks in before Calamares even loads, so you'll see the difference at the bootloader screen, not just inside the installer. And if you want encryption on a fresh install, do it from the Calamares "Encrypt system" toggle rather than expecting it to be on by default. That's the change Darren committed today, and it keeps you in control of the trade-off instead of guessing a passphrase at 1 AM.

— AcreetionOS newsletter, September 02, 2026
